title: The More of Less: Finding the Life You Want Under Everything You Own
author: Joshua Becker
target_audience: Adults and families interested in simplifying their lives
Readers overwhelmed by clutter and possessions
Individuals seeking more purpose, contentment, and freedom
Fans of minimalism and intentional living
core_themes: Minimalism as a path to greater fulfillment
Letting go of excess possessions to discover what truly matters
Redefining success and happiness beyond material accumulation
primary_purpose: To inspire readers to embrace minimalism by illustrating the profound benefits of owning less and to provide actionable advice for decluttering and creating a more meaningful, purposeful life.

structure_format.organization: Organized into thematically focused chapters blending narrative, reflection, and practical guidance
features: Personal stories from the author and others
Practical tips and steps for minimizing possessions
Discussion of common challenges and misconceptions

key_concepts_lessons: Owning less creates more space for purpose, joy, and meaningful relationships.
Clutter and consumerism distract from what is truly important in life.
Minimalism is not deprivation, but liberation from excess and distraction.
The decluttering process is both practical and deeply personal.
Minimalism benefits mental, emotional, and even financial well-being.
The journey toward minimalism looks different for everyone and can accommodate families and various lifestyles.
notable_features: Blends personal narrative with practical advice
Appeals to both beginners and those familiar with minimalism
Focuses on the deeper 'why' behind minimalism, not just 'how'
Addresses the emotional aspects of letting go of possessions
cultural_historical_context: Published in the mid-2010s during a rising interest in minimalism, simple living, and decluttering, the book reflects a societal pushback against rampant consumerism and an increasing desire for more intentional lifestyles.
reception_impact: Became a bestseller within the minimalism and self-help genres
Widely praised for its approachable style and practical wisdom
Inspired many to begin or deepen their journey into minimalism
Some critics argue that the advice may not address all socioeconomic backgrounds or extreme circumstances
comparable_titles: The Life-Changing Magic of Tidying Up by Marie Kondo
Essentialism: The Disciplined Pursuit of Less by Greg McKeown
Goodbye, Things: The New Japanese Minimalism by Fumio Sasaki
Minimalism: Live a Meaningful Life by Joshua Fields Millburn & Ryan Nicodemus
